title: Tool-calling safe-defaults: internal announce + Q&A scratch
content:
Purpose: rough personal notes for a short internal announcement (and accompanying Q&A crib) about changing the default behavior for tool/function calls in hosted API responses. This is a working draft — lots of TODOs and places where I want engineering/legal/product input.

Context (why this exists):
- Over the last 3 months we've seen increasing confusion and a few customer tickets about unexpected tool calls in streaming responses (primarily around plugins and structured-output tooling).
- Some customers expect 'tools are off unless explicitly requested' while others prefer aggressive tool suggestions for high automation. We need a safer, predictable default for hosted API and a clear comms path.
- This draft proposes a "safe-default" toggle flip for new accounts + a migration path for existing customers.

High-level change (simple bullet):
- New accounts: tool-calling is disabled by default. SDK/REST responses will not invoke tools unless the request explicitly sets tool_call: allowed or uses an invocation_scope param.
- Existing accounts: no immediate behavioral change. We will provide an optional migration step and a two-month opt-in period before switching an explicit default for accounts that have been inactive on settings.

Audience: internal first (engineers, sales, support, trust & safety, legal). We will iterate on a customer-facing announcement after feedback.

Key messages (for exec/PM to use in 2-min all-hands line and internal email):
- "We're prioritizing predictable defaults: starting now, new workspaces will have tool-calling off by default. This reduces accidental data exfil and aligns with conservative security expectations while preserving the power for teams that want automation."
- "No change to your current configuration — any teams currently using tool calls will continue to do so until they opt into the migration."
- "We will provide a one-click migration guide, SDK helpers, and migration logs to help you opt-in and audit behavior."

Suggested all-hands script (60–90s):
- opening: "Quick update on tool-calling defaults — small change, big safety upside."
- why: 1 sentence about observed confusion + risk; give an example (customer found an outbound webhook called unexpectedly when streaming large structured responses).
- what: explain new-account default and migration path for existing customers.
- reassure: no breaking changes, tooling to help migrate, docs + runbook coming.
- call to action for internal teams: support and sales please read the migration FAQ and escalate any customer concerns to the product triage channel.

Support/sales-facing FAQ crib (rough Q&A to refine):
Q: Will this break customers who rely on tool calls now?
A: No immediate changes to existing accounts. If a customer wants to test the new default, they can toggle in Console or set tool_call: allowed per-request. We'll provide explicit SDK flags (js/py) for quick local testing.

Q: How will we handle customers who say this reduces their product's value?
A: We will: 1) document the opt-in path; 2) offer migration help from Solutions Eng; 3) create a best-practices doc on safe patterns (explicit consent, sane retries, idempotency).

Q: Is this a security move or a product decision?
A: Both. It's primarily about predictability and tenant safety; legal/trust asked for a conservative default. Product designed the migration and dev-ex will ship SDK ergonomics.

Q: Timeline?
A: Draft timeline: announcements internally within 2 weeks; SDK flags and Console toggles in 3–4 weeks; migration guidance and customer blog + email in 6 weeks. Exact dates TBD.

Engineering notes / TODOs (technical constraints, for SRE/serving):
- Need a runtime flag at routing layer that checks account-level default and per-request override. Should be cheap to evaluate (token-level cost should not change).
- Streaming behavior: ensure that the early tool-decider hook doesn't cause partial streaming and then cancel; ideally decide tool invocation before any streaming tokens with tool intent are emitted.
- Audit logs: capture explicit tool_call decision per-request + which tool invoked + relevant metadata (region, model, request_id) for 90 days (or match account retention).
- Back-compat: any token-level tokenization/penalties? no. Keep model variants identical.

Talking points for Trust & Safety / Legal sync:
- Default-off reduces accidental outbound calls and external integrations being triggered without explicit intent.
- Migration path must not surface customer data to third parties without an active consent flow.
- Need templated terms/text for Console toggle and API docs reminding customers to check external integration scopes.

Open questions (please add):
- What is the exact UX in Console: name of toggle? ("Allow tool calls by default" vs "Enable tools for this workspace"). Which wording minimizes confusion?
- Do we provide a telemetry opt-out for experiments during rollout? (SRE/infra asks for toggles.)
- If a user sets tool_call: allowed per-request, do we record explicit consent in audit logs? (probably yes)

Immediate next steps (my personal todo):
- Share with PM (Raisa) and Trust & Safety (Noor) for quick feedback by EOD Friday.
- Draft a short internal email and a single-page migration guide for engineers (skeleton linked to the Confluence page above).
- Get engineering estimate for runtime flag + SDK flag by next Tuesday.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the customer-facing wording positive: "more control, same power". Avoid sounding like a slap on current customers.
- Might need a small demo script for Solutions Engs showing how to opt-in with the SDK in 30 seconds.
- If we do a gradual toggle flip for 'inactive' accounts, we need a clear list of what counts as inactive (no Console edits in 90 days? low API traffic?)

Draft internal email skeleton:
Subject: New default for tool-calling (internal heads-up)
Hi — short note: starting soon new workspaces will have tool-calling disabled by default. This reduces accidental external calls and aligns our defaults with conservative security practices. No action required for existing workspaces. We will publish a migration guide and SDK helpers in the next few weeks. Please read the FAQ and flag concerns in #product-tooling.

Sign-off: TBD (PM + Eng lead)

Final: this doc is messy — intended for quick iteration. If you're reading and have a strong word for the Console toggle naming or migration UX, add a line or DM me.

— Marisol
